attempts.raw_response: After fine grading, water the soil lightly to help it settle and create a better bond with the sod. Begin laying your sod along a straight edge, such as a sidewalk or driveway, and work your way outward. Stagger the joints in a brick-like pattern so the seams don't line up. Press the edges together tightly to avoid gaps. Once all the sod is laid, go over it with a lawn roller to ensure good contact between the roots and the soil. Water the newly laid sod thoroughly and keep it consistently moist for the first two weeks while the roots establish themselves.

pair.human_continuation:
If you’re working with a large area, it may be easier to use a lawn roller. Don’t pack down the soil too much or the roots on the sod won’t attach properly. The top .5 inches (1.3 cm) of soil should be loose enough that when you walk across the soil your feet leave .5 in (1.3 cm) footprints. Don’t lay down sod on dry soil or it won’t attach properly. You want the soil to be damp, not soaked. If you water the soil and it gets muddy, let it dry some before you lay down the sod.
Take an iron rake or shovel and break apart the high points in the soil.
pair.prefix: Avoid tilling the soil more than that or you could damage the structure of the soil. If you don’t own a rototiller, look up rototiller rentals near you and rent one for the day. Fine grading is the process of packing and smoothing the soil before you put the sod over it. Take a heavy mat and drag it over the surface of the soil several times until it’s smooth.
